tooltips.label: Sovereign Gold Bonds
tip: Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) are financial instruments issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on behalf of the Indian government. These bonds are a way for individuals to invest in gold without physically owning it.

tooltips.label: 2.5% P.A Interest on Amount
tip: Regular interest income of 2.5% pa payable half yearly in addition to capital appreciation on the value of gold.

tooltips.label: Stored in Digital Form
tip: Stored in a Demat form thus removing any risk of theft as compared if stored in physical form.

tooltips.label: Liquidity in Market
tip: Can be sold in secondary market once the lockin period is over.

tooltips.label: 0% capital gain tax
tip: Long Term Capital Gain (LTCG) tax is exempted if held till maturity, else taxed at 20% after indexation.

tooltips.label: Purity
tip: SGB purity is as per Gold bullion standards as compare to the questionable quality of physical gold.

tooltips.label: Government Securities
tip: Government securities (G-Secs) are financial instruments issued by a government to raise capital from investors, functioning as debt obligations backed by the government's credit.

tooltips.label: SEBI registered Debt broker
tip: SEBI registered broker is a brokerage firm authorized by India's Securities and Exchange Board to operate in the securities market, following the required regulations.

tooltips.label: G-Sec
tip: G-sec is a tradeable instrument issued by the Central Government or the State Governments. It acknowledges the Government’s debt obligation.

tooltips.label: NBFC
tip: NBFC or Non-Banking Financial Company is a financial institution that offers various banking services but doesn’t have the banking license to accept demand deposits.

tooltips.label: Payout
tip: Payout disbursement of funds, profits, or dividends to investors or stakeholders.

tooltips.label: KYC
tip: KYC or Know Your Customer is a process used by financial institutions to verify and authenticate the identity of the customers.
